title: Compatible affine square-zero lifts in the unramified lci Hilbert locus
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a morphism of stacks in groupoids on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site, def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]: isomorphism presheaves are sheaves and object descent is effective. Suppose $F$ is representable by algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], meaning that for every $S$-scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}h_T$ is an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. Assume each $X_y\to T$ is flat and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Fix $d\geq1$ and let $p_d:\mathcal L_d(F)\to\mathcal Y$ be the restricted forgetful functor [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids]. For every first order thickening $i:T_0\hookrightarrow T'$ of affine $S$-schemes [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], object $\xi_0\in\mathcal L_d(F)(T_0)$, object $y'\in\mathcal Y(T')$, and isomorphism $\gamma:p_d(\xi_0)\xrightarrow{\sim}y'|_{T_0}$, there are $\xi'\in\mathcal L_d(F)(T')$ and isomorphisms $a:\xi'|_{T_0}\xrightarrow{\sim}\xi_0$, $b:p_d(\xi')\xrightarrow{\sim}y'$ satisfying $b|_{T_0}=\gamma\circ p_d(a)$. In particular the finite locally free scheme of $\xi'$ has degree $d$ and its base change is the specified finite locally free scheme of $\xi_0$. No surjectivity of $F$ is required.

source.place: Tag 06D9 (lemma-lci-formally-smooth), using the unramified lci deformation of Tag 06D8 (lemma-lci-unobstructed).

proof.text: Write $\xi_0=(Z_0\xrightarrow{p_0}T_0,y_0,x_0,\alpha_0)$. Using $\gamma:y_0\simeq y'|_{T_0}$, replace the isomorphism component by $\beta_0=\alpha_0\circ(\gamma|_{Z_0})^{-1}$. The representing space $X'=X_{y'}$ has reduction $X_0=T_0\times_{T'}X'$, and $(x_0,\beta_0)$ defines $u_0:Z_0\to X_0$. This is unramified lci because it is the same Hilbert object after the given target isomorphism. By the Hilbert definition $p_0$ is finite locally free of degree $d$, hence flat and finite. Finiteness means affine, so $Z_0$ is affine over the affine $T_0$.

source.place: Tag 06D9 (lemma-lci-formally-smooth), reduction to the relative algebraic space; target isomorphism made explicit.

proof.text: Let $J$ be the ideal of $T_0\subset T'$ and $j:X_0\hookrightarrow X'$ its pullback. Since $X'\to T'$ is flat, the square-zero flatness criterion identifies $\mathcal C_{X_0/X'}$ canonically with the tensor pullback of $J$ to $X_0$. A closed immersion is formally unramified since it is a monomorphism, and $u_0$ is formally unramified by the universal-conormal result. Apply affine lci conormal splitting to $Z_0\to X_0\to X'$. Set $A=p_0^*J$ and $Q=\mathcal C_{Z_0/X_0}$. It gives $E=\mathcal C_{Z_0/X'}\simeq A\oplus Q$, with $A\to E$ the canonical conormal map. Pullback in two stages agrees with $p_0^*J$: on local tensors, $a\otimes(b\otimes t)\mapsto ab\otimes t$, inverse $a\otimes t\mapsto a\otimes(1\otimes t)$.

source.place: Tag 06D8 (lemma-lci-unobstructed), first and final paragraphs; conormal transitivity and flat base-change identification.

proof.text: The composite $Z_0\to X'$ is formally unramified: two maps to $Z_0$ over $X'$ have equal composites to $X_0$ because $X_0\to X'$ is a monomorphism, and equality of their reductions then forces equality by formal unramifiedness of $u_0$. Take its universal first-order thickening $Z_0\hookrightarrow W$ over $X'$, with ideal $E$. On its common etale topos with $Z_0$, put $H=s(Q)\subset E=A\oplus Q$. Since $E^2=0$, the $\mathcal O_W$ action on $E$ factors through $\mathcal O_{Z_0}$, so $H$ is an ideal of $\mathcal O_W$. The quotient $B=\mathcal O_W/H$ is a ring sheaf in an extension $0\to E/H\to B\to\mathcal O_{Z_0}\to0$, with square-zero quasi-coherent kernel $E/H\simeq A$. The scheme square-zero chart construction applied to this extension constructs a scheme $Z'$ with first-order closed immersion $Z_0\hookrightarrow Z'$ and identifies its entire etale ring sheaf with $B$.

source.place: Tag 06D8 (lemma-lci-unobstructed), middle paragraph, realizing its quotient ring sheaf by the scheme-chart construction of Tag 05YV.

proof.text: The identified etale topoi of $W$, $Z_0$ and $Z'$ give a ringed-topos morphism from $Z'$ to $W$ with ring map the quotient $\mathcal O_W\to B$. It is local: a local section of a ring with square-zero ideal is invertible exactly when its residue is, since if $ab=1+t$ with $t^2=0$ then $b(1-t)$ is an inverse of $a$. Apply space ringed-etale reconstruction to obtain a map $c:Z'\to W$. Work absolutely over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ using change-base-to-integers, which preserves the etale ringed sites. The composite $c|_{Z_0}$ and the original inclusion into $W$ induce the same ringed-topos map, so reconstruction's faithfulness makes them equal. Give $Z'$ the $S$-structure obtained by composing $c$ with $W\to S$. Set $u'=(W\to X')c$ and $p'=(X'\to T')u'$. Thus $u'$ really extends $u_0$, and its map on ideals is the quotient $E\to E/H$.

source.place: Tag 06D8 (lemma-lci-unobstructed), quotient construction; spaces-properties.tex Tag 04KL (theorem-fully-faithful) supplies the space morphism from its ringed-topos map.

proof.text: The canonical map $p_0^*J\to\mathcal C_{Z_0/Z'}$ for the composite $p':Z'\to X'\to T'$ is the canonical inclusion $A\xrightarrow{\lambda}E$ followed by $E\to E/H$. In the chosen splitting this is $a\mapsto(a,0)\bmod(0,Q)$, hence an isomorphism. Since $p_0$ is flat, the square-zero flatness criterion applied to $(Z_0\subset Z')\to(T_0\subset T')$ proves both that $p'$ is flat and that the canonical map $Z_0\to T_0\times_{T'}Z'$ is an isomorphism. This proves the prescribed reduction as a scheme-theoretic fibre product, rather than merely equality of the underlying spaces.

source.place: Tag 06D8 (lemma-lci-unobstructed), last paragraph: the retained conormal summand and the flatness criterion.

proof.text: The constructed $Z'$ is already a scheme. Apply finite-locally-free deformation to $p':Z'\to T'$ and its now-identified reduction $p_0$. It is finite locally free of degree $d$. In particular no lci claim about $u'$ or algebraicity of $\mathcal X$ or $\mathcal Y$ was needed to obtain the degree.

source.place: Tag 06D8 (lemma-lci-unobstructed), final sentence, after scheme realization of the quotient.

proof.text: By representability and the definition of the relative Hilbert groupoid, $u':Z'\to X_{y'}$ corresponds to $(x',\alpha':y'|_{Z'}\simeq F(x'))$. Thus $\eta=(Z'\to T',y',x',\alpha')$ is an object of $\mathcal H_d(F)(T')$. Apply the lci-open-locus theorem to $\eta$, obtaining $T^\circ\subset T'$. Its restriction to $T_0$ is the object of Step 1, so $T_0\to T'$ factors through $T^\circ$. A square-zero ideal lies in every prime, hence $|T_0|=|T'|$. Consequently the open $T^\circ$ contains every point of $T'$ and equals $T'$. Thus $\eta$ lies in $\mathcal L_d(F)(T')$; put $\xi'=\eta$.

The isomorphism $Z_0\simeq T_0\times_{T'}Z'$ and the reduction of $u'$ supply the scheme and $x$ components of $a:\xi'|_{T_0}\simeq\xi_0$. Choose its $y$ component to be $\gamma^{-1}$. The defining arrow equation in the Hilbert groupoid holds because the reduced isomorphism component was chosen as $\beta_0=\alpha_0\circ(\gamma|_{Z_0})^{-1}$ in Step 1. Take $b:p_d(\xi')\simeq y'$ to be the identity. Then $\gamma\circ p_d(a)=\gamma\circ\gamma^{-1}=1=b|_{T_0}$. These are precisely the required compatible isomorphisms. Surjectivity of $F$ has not been used.

source.place: Tag 06D9 (lemma-lci-formally-smooth), compatibility of the lifted object, with the given target isomorphism explicitly restored.

lean.statement: theorem exists_compatible_lci_lift {S : Scheme.{u}} {X : BasedCategory.{v₁, w₁} (Over S)} {Y : BasedCategory.{v₂, w₂} (Over S)} (F : BasedFunctor X Y) (hX : IsFppfModuliStack X) (hY : IsFppfModuliStack Y) (hF : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces F) (R : ∀ (T : Over S) (y : Functor.Fiber Y.p T), Representative (F := F) T y) (hflat : FlatLfp R) (d : ℕ+) (ξ₀ : Lci (d := d) hX hY hF R hflat) (T' : Over S) (i : ξ₀.obj.T ⟶ T') [IsAffine ξ₀.obj.T.left] [IsAffine T'.left] (hi : IsFirstOrderThickening i.left) (y' : Functor.Fiber Y.p T') (γ : ξ₀.obj.y.val ⟶ y'.val) (hγ : Y.p.IsHomLift i γ) : ∃ (ξ' : Lci (d := d) hX hY hF R hflat) (a : ξ₀.obj ⟶ ξ'.obj) (b : ξ'.obj.y.val ≅ y'.val), (base (F := F) (d := d)).IsHomLift i a ∧ Y.p.IsHomLift (𝟙 T') b.hom ∧ a.b ≫ b.hom = γ

The cartesian scheme square and degree d are retained in the existing Hilbert object and Hom structures. No statement correction or extra mathematical hypothesis.
